text:
Ana: follow-up from the postmortem: memcache alert storm caused three noisy pages last night. want to try a low-friction experiment to cut noise but keep visibility.
Mike: saw it too. most pages were one-off host spikes, low user impact.
Jia: what's the plan?
Ana: propose adding an SNR gate + probabilistic suppression layer in the pager. brief rules: only page if (threshold breached) AND (snr >= 0.65) OR if breach shows up on >=3 distinct hosts within 10m. if snr in [0.35,0.65], sample pages at 20% and always create internal tickets for suppressed cases.
Oliver: how are we computing snr?
Ana: computed from existing metrics: snr = (normalized_error_rate * normalized_traffic) / (1 + flap_index). it's cheap to compute from Prom/metrics backend at alert evaluation time or inside the pager middleware. low-volume flaps get low snr.
Mike: does this need infra changes?
Ana: two quick changes: 1) small Prom rule tweak + label to mark candidate pages, 2) pager middleware feature flag that calculates snr and applies probabilistic suppression. both are small PRs.
Jia: timeline?
Ana: target: open PR today, canary to staging tomorrow, prod deploy as a 72h experiment starting Mon 08:00 UTC. monitor pages, suppressed count, mttr, and user-error-rate.
Oliver: owner for rollout and rollback?
Ana: i'll own rollout and dashboards. Mike owns rollback steps and emergency revert. Jia will own runbook + ticketing integration.
SRE-Bot: auto-incident dump: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-452 (memcache miss spike at 2026-03-18T21:14Z).
Mike: rule change detail: keep current percentile thresholds for now, add the snr gate. don7t change the baseline percentile in this experiment.
Jia: sample rule snippet for ops repo:
```
alert: memcache_95p_latency_high
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(memcache_latency_bucket[5m])) > 0.2
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page_candidate
annotations:
  summary: "memcache 95th > 200ms (candidate)"
# Pager decision pseudocode:
# compute snr_score
# if (snr_score >= 0.65) || (distinct_hosts >= 3) || (persisting >= 15m) => page
# else if (0.35 <= snr_score < 0.65) => sample with p=0.20 (but always create ticket)
```
Ana: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-alerting/pull/417 contains the rule and test cases. middleware PR coming.
Oliver: what metrics define success/failure?
Ana: success: pages/day for memcache alerts drops ~50% without mttr rising more than 10% and user-facing errors stable. also verify suppressed alerts are logged and create tickets.
Mike: add rollback steps now for oncall: 1) toggle off pager middleware feature flag, 2) revert alert rule to previous commit, 3) if pages spike > baseline, escalate.
Jia: add an audit trail: every suppressed alert should write a record to /logs/alerts/suppressed and create a ticket with metadata for CS.
Ana: yes. middleware will emit structured logs and create a ticket with tag alert-suppressed.
SRE-Bot: scheduled experiment window: Mon 2026-03-22 08:00 UTC -> +72h. reminder 1h before deploy.
Oliver: ok. action items: Ana -> rollout + dashboards (due EOD Mon, with 24h checkpoints), Mike -> rollback doc + emergency runbook (due EOD today), Jia -> ticketing hooks + runbook update (due next Wed). reconvene Thu after experiment to review results. :thumbsup:
